messages.subject: Can I exclude one of the 8 founder strains in DO parental contribution mapping?
messages.subject_clean: Can I exclude one of the 8 founder strains in DO parental contribution mapping?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I am mapping the parental contributions to a specific QTL and the WSB effects are kind of blowing everything out. You had mentioned previously that this means that WSB does not have an allele call at all of these locations. Is there any way I can map the other 7 strains without including the WSB effects?

Thanks!

Sincerely,
Avni

messages.subject: GRCm38 Mbp location to cM
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

The genotyping array we used gives us only the Mbp location for all the SNPs. I know qtl2 utilizes cM to calculate the genotype probabilities. What else does qtl2 utilize the genetic location for?

In addition, I am going back and redoing the analysis for the purpose of more complete documentation. When I convert my Mbp locations to cM, which cM build should I use? Cox or G2F1?

Thanks!

Sincerely,
Avni

messages.body_plain:

Sorry for the barrage of questions... Is there a way to plot the full genotype probs (all chromosomes colored by parental strains) for a single individual. I see the function plot_genoprob, but I was looking for something like plot.genoprobs in the DOQTL package. If this is just the function you use, is there a way to export an individual's founder haplotype contributions at each SNP such that I can use DOQTL to make these plots?

Thanks!

Sincerely,
Avni

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Plotting genotype probs for a individual DO mouse
messages.body_plain:
> Sorry for the barrage of questions... Is there a way to plot the full
> genotype probs (all chromosomes colored by parental strains) for a
> single individual. I see the function plot_genoprob, but I was looking
> for something like plot.genoprobs in the DOQTL package. If this is
> just the function you use, is there a way to export an individual's
> founder haplotype contributions at each SNP such that I can use DOQTL
> to make these plots?

I've not found a way to depict the full genome for all individuals in a
way that is at all interpretable.
You can look at the genotype probabilities for one chromosome with
plot_genoprob(), or you can look at a genome reconstruction genome-wide
for one individual with plot_onegeno().

I'll take a look at plot.genoprobs in DOQTL.

The qtl2convert package (https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2convert) contains a
function probs_qtl2_to_doqtl() for converting genotype probabilities
from the R/qtl2 format to the DOQTL format.

karl

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Can I exclude one of the 8 founder strains in DO parental contribution mapping?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

So the reason I was asking about this was because I have often gotten plots like the first one below- where one founder strain (in this case WSB) blows everything out weirdly... So I just wanted to see what was happening under the surface, but I see the second graph...

So I tried to go back to the actual data instead of just censoring the graph. You had mentioned previously that this could be due to a particular founder having a null value at that SNP. So I went through in the pre-analysis and took out all the SNPs that had a single NA (about 16000 of our 400000 SNPs). Unfortunately, I got the third graph (same as first)...  One confounding factor is that this issue always occurs on Chromosome 2. Can you think of any other reason we could be seeing these wonky founder effects?

Thanks!

Sincerely,
Avni

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Can I exclude one of the 8 founder strains in DO parental contribution mapping?
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Can I exclude one of the 8 founder strains in DO parental contribution mapping?
messages.body_plain:
The problem is not that founder genotypes are missing, but rather than particular founder alleles are completely absent from the set of offspring. This becomes a bigger difficulty when the sample size is small for particular phenotypes. I don't have a ready solution to these problems at present, but will try to revise things to give more robust results in such cases. But I don't think I'll have time to work on this seriously until the fall.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Can I exclude one of the 8 founder strains in DO parental contribution mapping?
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Can I exclude one of the 8 founder strains in DO parental contribution mapping?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

Thank you for the clarification. We looked into this and apparently this is a section of the genome that Jackson Labs has intentionally removed all WSB contribution from because of a transmission ratio distortion issue. In case you are interested in learning more about this, this paper talks about the selection they made: "Diversity Outbred Mice at 21: Maintaining Allelic Variation in the Face of Selection", Chesler et al. 2016, G3.

In terms of my analysis, I'm planning on just introducing NULL values to the foundergeno file for WSB on Chr 2 for that section and rerunning the calcgenoprob functions. I feel like this is fine because none of the DOs will have any contribution from WSB in this section anyways. What do you think? Do you have a better way of looking at this?

Thanks,
Avni
